digest.component_or_area: store write lock (mkdir lock owner staleness)
propositions: On platforms without /proc (e.g. macOS), _process_start_time always returns None, causing the recycled-pid detection branch in _mkdir_lock_is_stale to be unsatisfiable and fall through to return False, resulting in unbounded lock wedging when a dead holder's pid is recycled by an unrelated live process

When _process_start_time returns None indicating an unqualified pid-liveness verdict, _mkdir_lock_is_stale now applies the 1h ceiling backstop; corroborated owners (matching start times) are never reclaimed on a timer, and already-proven-recycled pids (differing start times) are reclaimed immediately

A live owner holding the exclusive fcntl leg cannot be reached at the staleness check because _acquire_mkdir's precondition is the caller already holds that leg for the entire mkdir-leg lifetime; reaching the ceiling check is itself evidence the stamped owner let go, limiting blast radius to orphans only

The owner-identity/stamp/staleness/reclaim cluster was extracted from lock.py (798/800 LOC) to lock_owner.py to stay within the 200-800 LOC module-size limit, with lock.py calling lock_owner.py module-qualified to avoid creating multiple bindings that would break monkeypatching in tests
